title: RPSGT V3 PAP Modality Separation Map

questionBankSnapshot.action: No bulk question generation or question rewriting; strengthen pathway-specific authority routing.

policy: Classify the treatment pathway before applying PAP teaching. Adult OSA CPAP/APAP/BPAP guidance, adult CSA treatment/ASV context, and hypoventilation/NIV support are not interchangeable. Current AASM treatment/scoring authority leads; AAST supports technologist workflow where applicable; orders, facility SOPs, state/scope requirements, and current manufacturer labeling/instructions govern local/device-specific execution.

routes.label: Adult OSA PAP treatment and modality selection context
routes.boundary: This is the adult OSA route. Do not use it as current treatment authority for CSA/ASV or hypoventilation/NIV.

routes.label: Adult OSA CPAP/BPAP manual titration workflow
routes.boundary: Event-response and pressure-adjustment teaching belongs to OSA CPAP/BPAP titration. Do not generalize this algorithm to ASV or NIV modes.

routes.label: PAP education, interface, acclimation, adherence, and troubleshooting support
routes.boundary: Comfort, interface, communication, and adherence support may cross PAP modalities, but treatment selection and device settings remain indication-specific.

routes.label: Adult CSA PAP and ASV treatment context
routes.boundary: The 2025 AASM adult CSA guideline controls current clinical treatment context. ASV administration also requires the current label/IFU for the actual device. ResMed's current HFrEF/predominant-CSA contraindication is device-specific and must not be generalized across manufacturers; clinical guideline eligibility does not cancel a current device contraindication.

routes.label: Treatment-emergent central events during PAP
routes.boundary: Recognize and score the respiratory pattern with current AASM rules, then route treatment decisions through current CSA guidance and the ordered/facility workflow rather than simply escalating OSA pressure logic.

routes.label: Hypoventilation and NIV / ventilation-support pathway
routes.boundary: Teach ventilation and CO2 monitoring separately from OSA splinting. The AASM NPPV paper is active-listed but older and must be currentness-watched. Mode-specific NIV setup, backup-rate, target-volume, pressure-support, alarms and device operation require the current order, facility protocol, manufacturer instructions and diagnosis-specific guidance; do not infer a universal modern NIV algorithm from older NPPV or OSA PAP guidance.

routes.label: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome — CPAP versus NIV context
routes.boundary: ATS 2019 supplies current OHS-specific specialty support. Stable ambulatory OHS with severe OSA follows a CPAP-first branch rather than automatic NIV; NIV is used in other OHS circumstances according to clinician direction. Do not generalize the OHS pathway to every hypoventilation syndrome.

routes.label: Device-specific and facility-specific execution boundary
routes.boundary: The learner should know which pathway is being treated and what signals must be monitored, but contraindications, device menus, mode names, setup sequences, alarms, pressure limits, backup-rate settings and escalation thresholds may be manufacturer/facility specific and must not be hard-coded as universal rules.

explicitNonRules: Do not collapse CPAP, BPAP for OSA, ASV for CSA, and NIV for hypoventilation into one PAP algorithm.
Do not use the AAST manual OSA titration guideline as CSA/ASV treatment authority.
Do not use an OSA pressure-increase rule as a universal response to central events.
Do not treat a current AASM ASV treatment recommendation as overriding the contraindications or instructions for the actual ASV device being used.
Do not teach a universal NIV mode setup, backup rate, target volume, alarm, or pressure-support algorithm without an applicable current authoritative source plus order/facility/manufacturer context.
Generic PAP adherence and interface support does not establish treatment indication or modality selection.

remainingGaps.topic: Universal mode-specific NIV titration protocol within the audited authority registry
remainingGaps.handling: Use the active-listed AASM NPPV framework with currentness warning plus scoring/CO2 authority, and preserve the order/facility/manufacturer boundary rather than inventing settings.
Current ResMed AirCurve 11 ASV labeling is mapped as one device overlay; verify the actual device label/IFU rather than generalizing ResMed rules.
